{{nihongo|'''Ai Shrine'''|阿為神社}} is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}{{ill|Ibaraki, Osaka|Q502403|qid=Q502403}}{{ill|Ai|ja|安威村|ko|아이촌 (오사카부)|uk|Ай (Осака)|qid=Q11450514|lt=Awi}}. {{nihongo|'''Ai Shrine'''|阿為神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].
It is a Shikinaisha listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, recorded as “{{ill|Settsu Province|ca|Província de Settsu|cs|Provincie Seccu|de|Provinz Settsu|eo|Provinco Seccu|es|Provincia de Settsu|fa|ولایت ستسو|fr|Province de Settsu|gl|Provincia de Settsu|hak|Settsu-koet|id|Provinsi Settsu|it|Settsu (provincia)|ja|摂津国|ko|셋쓰국|lt|Seccu žemė|nl|Settsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Settsu|ru|Сэтцу (провинция)|simple|Settsu Province|sk|Seccu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сецу|tr|Settsu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сеццу|zh|攝津國|zh_min_nan|Settu-kok|zh_yue|攝津國|qid=Q864163}}{{ill|Shimashimo district|ja|島下郡|zh|岛下郡|qid=Q10976940}} Ai Shrine, Kuwabuki.” It is also known as Naemori Shrine.

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, it is an ancient shrine said to have been founded by the enshrinement carried out by {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|Q433995|qid=Q433995}}. In the “Settsu Shinbetsu” section of the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}, it states: “Nakatomi Aino Muraji, same deity ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508|lt=Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto}}), descendant in the twelfth generation of Ōe no Omi,” indicating that the Nakatomi Aino clan enshrined their ancestral deity here.

* Meiji 40 ({{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}}), January: Designated as a shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and ritual implements.
* April 5, Meiji 40: A heihaku shrine was merged into the shrine.
* Meiji 41 ({{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}}): The Shikinaisha '''{{ill|Mitekura Shrine|Q11481884|qid=Q11481884}}''' was merged.
* Heisei 17 ({{ill|2005|Q2019|qid=Q2019}}): The main hall was newly constructed. As a commemorative event for its completion, a sacred ritual of {{ill|Kemari|Q12224003|qid=Q12224003}}, closely associated with Fujiwara no Kamatari, was dedicated. Since then, the “Kemari Gathering” has been held annually every November.<ref>[https://dainenji.jimdofree.com/%E3%83%96%E3%83%AD%E3%82%B0-1/%E9%98%BF%E7%82%BA%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/%E9%98%BF%E7%82%BA%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%E8%B9%B4%E9%9E%A0%E3%81%AE%E4%BC%9A/ Ai Shrine Kemari Gathering] – Jōdo sect {{ill|Dainen-ji Temple|Q11435458|qid=Q11435458|lt=Dainen-ji}} website</ref>.
